Abstract base class providing a portable interface to a system thread. Derive from Thread and implement run() to define the thread’s work. Call start() to create and run the thread; join() waits for completion; joinable() reports if the thread can be joined. The destructor joins/destroys the thread. Copy and move are disabled. Internally uses std::thread when ILMTHREAD_THREADING_ENABLED is true. Note: due to potential race with object destruction and run() start, users should synchronize (e.g., with a semaphore) to ensure run() has started before destruction, as described in the header comments.

origin and w should correspond to the image/data window and width used for indexing. [inferred]

functions.description: Reads a block of raw (compressed) scanline data starting at firstScanLine without decompressing it, returning a pointer to internal storage and its size. Intended to support fast pixel copying routines (e.g., OutputFile::copyPixels()).
requirements: firstScanLine should be a valid scanline within the file’s data window; exact block sizing semantics are not specified here.
On return, pixelData points to memory owned by the InputFile; the pointer’s lifetime and reuse across calls are not specified here (treat as temporary/invalidated by subsequent calls).
pixelDataSize is set to the size in bytes of the returned raw block.

functions.name: InputFile::rawPixelDataToBuffer
functions.signature: void InputFile::rawPixelDataToBuffer(int scanLine, char* pixelData, int& pixelDataSize) const
functions.description: Reads one scanline’s worth of raw (compressed) data for scanLine into a caller-provided buffer without decompressing it. Enables decoupling IO from decompression for external threading.
requirements: scanLine must lie within [header().dataWindow().min.y, header().dataWindow().max.y].

Caller must provide a pre-allocated buffer pixelData with capacity of at least pixelDataSize bytes; on return, pixelDataSize is set to the actual number of bytes written. The method of determining required capacity prior to the call is not specified here.
pixelData must be writable and valid for at least pixelDataSize bytes.

functions.name: InputFile::rawTileData
functions.signature: void InputFile::rawTileData(int& dx, int& dy, int& lx, int& ly, const char*& pixelData, int& pixelDataSize)
functions.description: Reads a tile of raw (compressed) pixel data without decompressing it, returning tile coordinates (dx,dy), level coordinates (lx,ly), and a pointer to internal storage with its size. Intended to support TiledOutputFile::copyPixels().
requirements: Intended for tiled data; specific preconditions (iteration order, valid ranges for dx/dy/lx/ly) are not specified here.
On return, pixelData points to memory owned by the InputFile; pointer lifetime is not specified (treat as temporary/invalidated by subsequent calls).
pixelDataSize is set to the size in bytes of the returned raw tile block.

functions.name: OutputFile::OutputFile
functions.signature: OutputFile(const char fileName[], const Header& header, int numThreads = globalThreadCount());
functions.description: Constructs an OutputFile, opens the target file by name, and writes the provided file header. The header is copied into the OutputFile and is later accessible via header(). Destroying this OutputFile automatically closes the file. numThreads controls the number of worker threads used when writing.
requirements: fileName must point to a valid, null-terminated path string to a file that can be created/opened for writing.
header must describe the image to be written; it is copied into the OutputFile upon construction.
Call setFrameBuffer() at least once before calling writePixels().
To produce a complete/correct file, exactly m scan lines must be written, where m = header().dataWindow().max.y - header().dataWindow().min.y + 1.
Destroying the OutputFile before writing all required scan lines will produce an incomplete file.
numThreads determines the number of threads used (see ImfThreading.h); specific bounds are not stated in this header (unknown).

functions.name: OutputFile::~OutputFile
functions.description: Destructor. Closes the file automatically for file-based construction; does not close an externally supplied OStream. Destroying the object before all scan lines are written results in an incomplete file.
requirements: Ensure all required scan lines have been written (exactly m as defined by the data window) before destruction to avoid an incomplete file.
If constructed with an external OStream, the caller is responsible for closing/disposing the stream.

functions.name: OutputFile::fileName
functions.description: Returns the name of the file associated with this OutputFile. Useful for diagnostics and logging. For stream-based construction, behavior is not documented in this header (may be unknown or implementation-defined).
requirements: Returned pointer is owned by the OutputFile; do not free it (implied by returning const char*; explicit lifetime details are unknown).
Value may be unknown/unspecified when constructed with an OStream (not documented here).

functions.name: OutputFile::header
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the file header that was written at construction time and copied into the OutputFile. Use this to query attributes such as dataWindow, compression, lineOrder, and channels.
requirements: Do not attempt to modify the returned Header (const).
Assumes the OutputFile remains alive while using the returned reference.

functions.name: OutputFile::setFrameBuffer
functions.description: Sets the current frame buffer by copying the provided FrameBuffer object into the OutputFile. The current frame buffer supplies pixel data to writePixels(). It may be changed between writePixels() calls.
requirements: Must be called at least once before the first call to writePixels().
frameBuffer must be initialized and describe the source pixel data layout expected by the file header’s channels and data window (exact matching rules not detailed here; some specifics are unknown).
Any pointers/slices referenced by the FrameBuffer must remain valid for the duration of the writes that use them (implied; explicit lifetime rules not detailed here).

functions.name: OutputFile::frameBuffer
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the current frame buffer stored in the OutputFile. Use to inspect which pixel slices are configured for writing.
requirements: The returned reference is only valid while the OutputFile object exists.
Do not modify through this const reference.

functions.name: OutputFile::writePixels
functions.description: Writes the next numScanLines scan lines from the current frame buffer into the file, starting at currentScanLine() and proceeding according to header.lineOrder(). Call repeatedly until the entire data window has been written.
requirements: setFrameBuffer() must have been called at least once prior to writePixels().
numScanLines defaults to 1; it should be a positive integer (non-positive values are not documented/unsupported; behavior unknown).
Across all calls, exactly m scan lines must be written, where m = header().dataWindow().max.y - header().dataWindow().min.y + 1, to produce a complete and correct file.
Writing fewer than m lines before destruction will result in an incomplete file.

functions.name: OutputFile::currentScanLine
functions.description: Returns the y coordinate of the next scan line that writePixels() will write from the current frame buffer, advancing after each scan line according to the header’s lineOrder (increasing or decreasing Y).
requirements: None beyond having a valid OutputFile; interpretation depends on header().lineOrder().

functions.name: OutputFile::copyPixels
functions.description: Copies all pixel data from an InputFile into this OutputFile without decompressing and recompressing the data. Use as a fast path when headers are compatible.
requirements: The headers must be compatible: dataWindow, compression, lineOrder, and channels must be identical between this file and the InputFile.
in must remain valid for the duration of the copy.
The destination OutputFile must be in a state ready to receive all scan lines (overall requirement to write exactly m lines still applies).

functions.name: OutputFile::copyPixels
functions.description: Copies all pixel data from an InputPart (multipart input) into this OutputFile, equivalent in intent to copyPixels(InputFile&) but for multipart inputs. Avoids decompressing and recompressing the data when headers are compatible.
requirements: The headers must be compatible: dataWindow, compression, lineOrder, and channels must be identical between this file and the InputPart.
in must remain valid for the duration of the copy.
The destination OutputFile must be in a state ready to receive all scan lines (overall requirement to write exactly m lines still applies).

functions.name: OutputFile::updatePreviewImage
functions.description: Updates the preview image attribute in the file’s header with a new set of PreviewRgba pixels. Intended for cases where the preview image is only known after writing the main image data. Throws IEX_NAMESPACE::LogicExc if the header has no preview image attribute.
requirements: The file’s header must contain a preview image attribute; otherwise this call throws a LogicExc.
newPixels must point to at least as many pixels as the preview image expects (exact dimensions/length derived from the header’s preview image attribute; exact size not stated here).
Call only after the file is open; can be called after writing scan lines as needed to update the embedded preview.

functions.name: Image::Image
functions.description: Default constructor for Image. Initializes an empty image container with no levels and an empty data window; channels may be added later. Actual initialization details are internal to the implementation.

functions.name: Image::~Image
functions.description: Virtual destructor for Image. Cleans up image levels, channels, and associated resources.

functions.name: Image::levelMode
functions.description: Returns the image’s level mode (ONE_LEVEL, MIPMAP_LEVELS, or RIPMAP_LEVELS). Use this to determine how many levels exist and how to interpret level indices.

functions.name: Image::levelRoundingMode
functions.description: Returns the rounding mode (ROUND_UP or ROUND_DOWN) used when computing per-level sizes and level counts.

functions.name: Image::numLevels
functions.description: Convenience accessor returning the number of levels for ONE_LEVEL and MIPMAP_LEVELS images. For RIPMAP_LEVELS images, this function is not applicable and throws LogicExc.
requirements: Caller must be prepared to handle a LogicExc exception when levelMode() == RIPMAP_LEVELS.

functions.name: Image::numXLevels
functions.description: Returns the number of levels in the x direction, computed from the image data window, level mode, and rounding mode as documented in the header comments.

functions.name: Image::numYLevels
functions.description: Returns the number of levels in the y direction, computed from the image data window, level mode, and rounding mode as documented in the header comments.

functions.name: Image::dataWindow
functions.description: Returns the image’s data window, which is the same as the data window for level (0, 0).

functions.name: Image::dataWindowForLevel
functions.description: Returns the data window for level (l, l). Provided as a convenience for ONE_LEVEL and MIPMAP_LEVELS images; on RIPMAP_LEVELS this refers to the diagonal level if it exists.
requirements: l must be a valid level index for both x and y axes (0 <= l < numXLevels() and 0 <= l < numYLevels()).

functions.name: Image::levelWidth
functions.description: Returns the width of a level with level number (lx, *), using max(1, rfunc(w / 2^lx)) where rfunc is determined by the rounding mode. Width is computed from the base data window width.
requirements: lx must be in the range [0, numXLevels()).

functions.name: Image::levelHeight
functions.description: Returns the height of a level with level number (*, ly), using max(1, rfunc(h / 2^ly)) where rfunc is determined by the rounding mode. Height is computed from the base data window height.
requirements: ly must be in the range [0, numYLevels()).

functions.name: Image::resize
functions.description: Resizes the image to the given data window, preserving the current level mode and rounding mode. Allocates new storage for levels and channels; contents are discarded.
requirements: Caller should not rely on preserving any existing pixel data; all pixel data are lost on resize.
If allocation fails, the image will end up with an empty data window and no levels; caller must be prepared to handle this state.

functions.name: Image::shiftPixels
functions.description: Shifts all pixels and the image data window by (dx, dy). No pixel data are lost; only coordinates change. Throws ArgExc if the shift distances are incompatible with channel sampling.
requirements: dx must be a multiple of every channel’s xSampling.
dy must be a multiple of every channel’s ySampling.
Caller must be prepared to handle an ArgExc exception if the sampling divisibility requirement is violated.

functions.name: Image::insertChannel
functions.signature: void Image::insertChannel(const std::string& name, PixelType type, int xSampling = 1, int ySampling = 1, bool pLinear = false)
functions.description: Inserts or replaces a channel in the image with the given name, pixel type, sampling rates, and perceptual linearity flag. If a channel with the same name exists it is deleted before adding the new one.
requirements: If a channel with the same name already exists, it will be removed and replaced.
xSampling should be a positive integer (inferred from the definition of sampling rates).
ySampling should be a positive integer (inferred from the definition of sampling rates).

functions.name: Image::eraseChannel
functions.description: Erases the channel with the given name from the image. No-op if the channel does not exist (no behavior specified otherwise).

functions.name: Image::clearChannels
functions.description: Erases all channels from the image.

functions.name: Image::renameChannel
functions.signature: void Image::renameChannel(const std::string& oldName, const std::string& newName)
functions.description: Renames the channel oldName to newName. Throws ArgExc if oldName does not exist or newName already exists. On out-of-memory during renaming, the channel being renamed is erased and an exception is thrown.
requirements: oldName must name an existing channel.
newName must not conflict with any existing channel name.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets a generic string data type that is consumed by many
# fuzzer stubs via FUZZ_PARAM_STR (std::string) and sometimes as C-strings.
# The stubs typically sanitize to printable ASCII, enforce non-empty, and bound
# lengths (commonly 16, 64, 128, 256). They also exercise special tokens such as
# channel names for FrameBuffer and the specific token "unknown" for colorInteropID.
#
# Strategy
# - Produce a sequence of length-prefixed strings that the fuzz harness can draw from
#   when it calls FUZZ_PARAM_STR repeatedly.
# - Include a diversity of values: empty, short printable, long bounded, unicode-like
#   (UTF-8), names relevant to channels, and the special token "unknown".
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Deterministic per seed but varied across calls.
#
# Encoding format (simple, self-describing):
#   [u16 count][ repeated entries: u16 len | bytes... ]
# The fuzzer’s FUZZ_PARAM_STR will typically slice sequentially from the buffer.
# Providing a structured list of strings ensures each call sees a sensible value.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand_printable(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Printable ASCII 32..126
    return ''.join(r.choice(string.printable[:94]) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_identifier(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    first = r.choice(string.ascii_letters + '_')
    rest_len = r.randint(max(0, min_len-1), max_len-1)
    rest_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '_'
    rest = ''.join(r.choice(rest_chars) for _ in range(rest_len))
    return first + rest

def _rand_utf8(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Mix ASCII and some multi-byte sequences
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < n:
        mode = r.randint(0, 9)
        if mode < 6:
            out.append(r.randint(32, 126))
        elif mode < 8:
            # 2-byte UTF-8
            ch = r.randint(0x00A0, 0x07FF)
            out.extend(chr(ch).encode('utf-8'))
        else:
            # 3-byte UTF-8
            ch = r.randint(0x0800, 0x2FFF)
            out.extend(chr(ch).encode('utf-8'))
        if len(out) > max_len:
            break
    return out[:max_len].decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')

def _bounded(r: random.Random, s: str, max_len: int) -> str:
    if len(s) > max_len:
        return s[:max_len]
    return s

def _unique_append(lst: List[str], s: str):
    if s not in lst:
        lst.append(s)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    strings: List[str] = []

    # Core tokens
    _unique_append(strings, "")  # empty for places where code handles empty specially
    _unique_append(strings, "unknown")  # used by colorInteropID
    # Common short names/keys
    for tok in ["C", "A", "K", "Chan", "ConstChan", "ConstSlice", "ConstView", "left", "right", "view"]:
        _unique_append(strings, tok)

    # Channel-like identifiers and header keys
    for _ in range(6):
        _unique_append(strings, _rand_identifier(r, 1, r.randint(3, 12)))

    # Printable strings within common bounds (16, 64, 128, 256)
    for maxlen in [16, 64, 128, 256]:
        _unique_append(strings, _bounded(r, _rand_printable(r, 1, maxlen), maxlen))
        _unique_append(strings, _bounded(r, _rand_printable(r, max(1, maxlen//2), maxlen), maxlen))
        _unique_append(strings, _bounded(r, _rand_utf8(r, 1, maxlen), maxlen))

    # Some longer comments/owner-style strings (up to 256)
    for _ in range(4):
        _unique_append(strings, _bounded(r, _rand_printable(r, 10, 256), 256))

    # Camera/lens attributes typical values
    for tok in [
        "Canon", "Nikon", "Sony", "ARRI", "RED", "FUJIFILM", "Panasonic",
        "EF 24-70mm f/2.8L", "Zeiss Planar T*", "SN123456", "FW1.2.3",
        "Owner Name", "Test Reel", "RenderingX", "LookModY"
    ]:
        _unique_append(strings, tok)

    # A few variations that deliberately collide or differ by suffix
    base = _rand_identifier(r, 1, 8)
    for suf in ["", "_x", "_miss", "_alt", "_01"]:
        _unique_append(strings, base + suf)

    # Ensure at least ~40-80 entries for multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    target_count = r.randint(40, 80)
    while len(strings) < target_count:
        choice = r.randint(0, 4)
        if choice == 0:
            s = _rand_identifier(r, 1, r.randint(4, 16))
        elif choice == 1:
            s = _bounded(r, _rand_printable(r, 1, 64), 64)
        elif choice == 2:
            s = _bounded(r, _rand_utf8(r, 1, 128), 128)
        elif choice == 3:
            s = r.choice(["left", "right", "view", "unknown", "owner", "comments"]) + str(r.randint(0, 99))
        else:
            s = base + "_" + _rand_identifier(r, 1, 6)
        _unique_append(strings, s)

    # Serialize into length-prefixed blob with u16 count and u16 lengths
    # Truncate if exceeding MAX_TOTAL
    out = bytearray()
    # Reserve space for count
    out.extend(b"\x00\x00")

    count = 0
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8')
        if len(b) > 65535:
            b = b[:65535]
        entry = len(b).to_bytes(2, 'little') + b
        if 2 + len(out) + len(entry) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out.extend(entry)
        count += 1

    # Write count
    out[0:2] = count.to_bytes(2, 'little')

    return bytes(out)

import os
import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for filesystem path inputs used by fuzzer stubs that create/read EXR files.
# The stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() to obtain a path for creating a temporary
# RgbaOutputFile and for opening with RgbaInputFile. We generate plausible, valid
# filesystem paths as bytes. The content addressed by the path will be created by
# the stub itself; we only need to provide a syntactically valid path string.
#
# Strategy:
# - Produce a mix of relative and nested paths.
# - Include various file name patterns (.exr, no extension, hidden files, spaces, unicode).
# - Occasionally include parent directories (./, ../) and platform-esque variations.
# - Keep under 4096 bytes and avoid characters likely to be rejected by most filesystems.
# - Ensure directories in the path are relative (no actual IO here) — the harness
#   will typically create the file. We avoid absolute paths and drive letters to
#   prevent permission/sandbox issues.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ ."

UNICODE_FRAGMENTS = [
    "π", "ß", "Ω", "漢", "字", "한", "글", "😀", "ñ", "ç", "ø", "å", "Ž", "ł",
]

EXTENSIONS = [".exr", ".EXR", ".rgba.exr", "", ".tmp.exr"]

REL_PREFIXES = ["", "./", "../", "././", ".././", "./tmp/", "./out/", "../build/"]

DIR_NAMES = [
    "images", "testdata", "data", "frames", "rgba", "yca", "yc", "tiny",
    "spaces in name", ".hidden", "demo-01", "Álpha", "实验", "テスト", "mix-π",
]

BASENAMES = [
    "img", "frame", "rgba", "y_only", "tile", "scanline", "min", "max",
    "case test", "hidden", ".exrfile", "😀_image", "long-name-with-dashes",
]


def _rand(r: random.Random, seq: List[str]) -> str:
    return seq[r.randrange(len(seq))]


def _rand_token(r: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=16) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = "".join(r.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n)).strip()
    # Ensure non-empty after strip
    if not s:
        s = "x"
    # Occasionally inject a unicode fragment at either end
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        s = r.choice(UNICODE_FRAGMENTS) + s
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        s = s + r.choice(UNICODE_FRAGMENTS)
    return s


def _build_relative_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    prefix = _rand(r, REL_PREFIXES)

    # Build 0-3 nested directories.
    depth = r.randint(0, 3)
    parts = []
    for _ in range(depth):
        if r.random() < 0.6:
            parts.append(_rand(r, DIR_NAMES))
        else:
            parts.append(_rand_token(r))

    # Choose basename and extension
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        base = _rand(r, BASENAMES)
    else:
        base = _rand_token(r)

    # Occasionally add frame index or dimensions
    suffix_bits = []
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        suffix_bits.append(f"_{r.randint(0, 9999):04d}")
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        w = r.randint(1, 64)
        h = r.randint(1, 64)
        suffix_bits.append(f"_{w}x{h}")

    ext = _rand(r, EXTENSIONS)

    filename = base + "".join(suffix_bits) + ext

    # Join path components with '/'
    path = prefix + "/".join([p for p in parts if p])
    if path and not path.endswith('/'):
        path += '/'
    path += filename

    # Normalize redundant slashes (keep leading ./ or ../ intact)
    while '//' in path:
        path = path.replace('//', '/')

    # Ensure not exceeding length limits for safety
    if len(path) > 4000:
        path = path[:4000]

    # Avoid path ending with slash
    if path.endswith('/'):
        path += "file.exr"

    return path


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # With small probability, emit just a simple filename to test minimal case.
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        name = _rand(r, BASENAMES) + _rand(r, EXTENSIONS)
        return name.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')[:4096]

    path = _build_relative_path(r)

    # Ensure we have an .exr suffix sometimes to guide libraries that inspect extension
    if not path.lower().endswith('.exr') and r.random() < 0.7:
        # Append .exr if no extension or if it seems arbitrary
        if '.' not in os.path.basename(path):
            path += '.exr'
        elif not path.lower().endswith('.exr'):
            path += '.exr'

    # Return as bytes
    b = path.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    return b[:4096]
